title: Shoreline: Compact Route Health & Model Ledger for Console
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Design a compact, glanceable per-route / per-model mini-dashboard (codenamed Shoreline) for the Redwood Console. This ticket captures the UX and chart-specs for a single-row ‘model ledger’ used inside route lists and rollout panes. The ledger must surface latency (p50/p95/p99), throughput (rps), token metrics (avg tokens/request, token waterfall), 
and cost signals at a glance, plus a small canary/rollout visualization. The goal is a high-information, low-real-estate component 
that lets engineers and PMs detect regressions, compare model variants, and drill into traces with one click.
acceptance_criteria: A compact ledger UI prototype exists in Figma showing: latency sparkline with p50/p95/p99, throughput sparkline, avg tokens, token waterfall thumbnail, cost-per-1M-token badge, and a canary traffic split bar.
Chart specs include aggregation windows (1m,5m,1h) and default time windows (1h/6h/24h) with clear documentation for p50/p95/p99 calculation and missing-data handling.
Compact mode renders legibly at 280px row height and mobile-responsive down to 320px width (graceful collapse to two-line layout).
Rollout visualization supports up to 4 model variants, shows live traffic % and an indicator for automated fallback policies.
Prototype annotated with accessibility contrast checks and tooltip text for each metric; design reviewed and approved by PM and Eng leads.
Linkable drill targets (Trace view, Full Route Dashboard, GitHub PR) are included in the prototype and documented in the design note.
decisions: Use a compact sparkline + micro-legend for latency with filled band for p95->p99 to convey tail behavior without requiring a full pane.
Throughput will be an underlaid area chart behind a line to preserve vertical space while still showing volume changes.
Token waterfall is rendered as an anchored micro-bar (bucketed by token range) with hover to expand to full waterfall in the drill view.
Default time windows will be 1h/6h/24h; short-term (1h) is default in route lists to highlight recent regressions.
Color palette reuses console semantic colors (success/warning/error) for thresholds; neutral blue for baseline p50, amber for p95, red for p99.
Canary traffic visualization uses small stacked bars with variant color swatches and a live percentage label; variants with <1% traffic are dimmed.
Cost signal displayed as normalized cost-per-1M-tokens badge (USD) with a small sparkline; cost calc documented in design note (includes batching adjustments).
tradeoffs: Condensing p50/p95/p99 into a single micro-chart reduces absolute precision but increases signal-to-noise for regression detection.
Showing cost estimates in the ledger requires pulling pre-aggregated pricing data which may lag by up to 2 minutes; documented to users as eventual consistency.
Including token waterfall detail inline would exceed row height; decided to keep thumbnail with hover-to-expand to full waterfall view.
Compact mode hides quantization overlay by default to avoid visual clutter; advanced users can toggle it in the expanded dashboard.
next_steps: Address Eng feedback on data-availability for 1m aggregation (ENG sync scheduled 2025-02-12).
Build HTML/CSS microcomponent spec and handoff tokens for dev (Liam to pick up after design review).
Implement accessibility pass (contrast and keyboard focus) and test with assistive tech.
Kick off a small usability session with 6 Platform engineers to validate glanceability (session planned 2025-02-17).
